declarations.description:
Guided product tour: walks a user through a page one element at a time, dimming everything else and explaining the
highlighted element in a panel beside it. Use it for onboarding and for introducing a new feature in place.

Each step is a `c2-tour-step` child naming its `target` (a CSS selector), a `heading` and the explanation as its
content. Put a button in the `trigger` slot, set `open` or call `start()` to begin; the panel offers Back, Next (Done on the last step) and a close
button, and shows the progress as "2 of 5". The target is scrolled into view when it is off screen, and the panel is
placed beside it by floating-ui, flipping to the other side when there is no room. A step without a target, or
whose target is missing, shows centred over the dimmed page.

The tour is a non-modal `dialog` in the top layer: the page stays interactive, so a step can ask the user to try
the highlighted control. Opening moves focus to Next; Escape and the close button end the tour early, and the
arrow keys move between steps while focus is in the panel. When it closes, focus returns to where it was before.

With a `storage-key`, the tour remembers in `localStorage` whether the user finished it, skipped it or got part
way, and on which step (`progress`). Add `autostart` to open it by itself on the first visit: it then resumes on the
step it was left on, and stays closed once finished or skipped. `start()` and the trigger always open it; `reset()`
forgets the stored progress.

Every tour a user ends fires exactly one `finish` (Done on the last step) or `skip` (Skip, the close button or Escape).
Moving between steps with the buttons, the keys or the methods fires `step-change`; setting `open` or `current`
from code fires only `show` / `hide`.

cssParts.description: The highlighted cut-out around the target; its shadow dims the rest of the page.
cssParts.name: spotlight

cssParts.description: The row holding the heading and the close button.
cssParts.name: header

cssParts.description: The button that ends the tour early.
cssParts.name: close

cssParts.name: body

cssParts.name: footer

cssParts.name: previous

slots.description: The `c2-tour-step` elements, in order. Only the current step is shown, inside the panel.
Optional button that starts the tour from its first step when clicked. It stays where the tour is placed.
slots.name: trigger

members.name: open
members.description: Visible state. Set it, or call `start()`, to begin the tour; setting it fires `show` / `hide` but no `finish` or `skip`.

members.name: current
members.description: Index of the step shown, from 0. Setting it moves the tour without firing `step-change`.

members.name: placement
members.description: Preferred side of the target for the panel; a step's own `placement` wins. Flips when there is no room.

members.name: storageKey
members.description:
`localStorage` key under which the tour remembers its progress (`{ "status", "step" }`). Empty, nothing is stored.
Use one key per tour, and a new key when a tour changes enough to be worth showing again.

members.name: autostart
members.description:
Opens the tour by itself when it is connected, unless the progress under `storage-key` says it was finished or
skipped. It resumes on the stored step. Without a `storage-key` it opens on every page load.

members.name: progress
members.description: The progress stored under `storage-key`: `new` when nothing is stored, the key is empty or storage is unavailable.

members.name: reset
members.description: Forgets the progress stored under `storage-key`, so `autostart` opens the tour again on the next load.

members.name: steps
members.description: The `c2-tour-step` children, in order.

members.name: currentStep
members.description: The step shown while open: `current`, kept within the steps.

members.name: start
members.description: Opens the tour on step `index` (the first by default).

members.name: next
members.description: Moves to the next step, or finishes the tour on the last one.

members.name: previous
members.description: Moves back one step.

members.name: goTo
members.description: Moves to step `index`, firing `step-change` when that is another step.

members.name: finish
members.description: Closes the tour as completed, firing `finish`.

members.name: skip
members.description: Closes the tour before its end, firing `skip`.

members.name: visibleTarget
members.description: The target when it is rendered, else `null` so the step shows centred.

events.name: step-change
events.description: The user, or a method, moved to another step. `detail.index` is the new step, `detail.previous` the old one.

events.name: finish
events.description: The user completed the tour with Done on the last step.

events.name: skip
events.description: The user ended the tour early with Skip, the close button or Escape. `detail.index` is the step it was closed on.

declarations.description:
One step of a `c2-tour`: the element it points at, a heading and the text that explains it. The step draws nothing
on its own; its tour shows the current step inside its panel, beside the highlighted target.

`target` is a CSS selector, looked up from the tour's root (the document, or the shadow root the tour sits in) when
the step is shown. A step without a target, or whose target is missing or not rendered, shows centred on a fully
dimmed page: use one for a welcome or closing step.
declarations.name: TourStep

slots.description: The step's explanation: a sentence, a list, an image. It is the tour panel's accessible description.

members.name: target
members.description: CSS selector of the element this step highlights. Empty, or matching nothing visible, the step shows centred.

members.name: heading
members.description: The step's title, shown at the top of the panel and used as its accessible name.

members.name: placement
members.description: Preferred side of the target for the panel, overriding the tour's `placement`; flips when there is no room.

members.name: targetElement
members.description: The element `target` selects right now, or `null`.
